answer: Each agent must post a bond in a scarce, externally costly resource before it can submit claims or earn rewards; when a claim is disproved by a randomly selected, independently bonded auditor, the claimant loses its bond and the auditor receives part. Splitting one identity into a comet trail of aliases does not multiply influence: every alias needs its own bond, while shared control risks correlated claims being exposed by a ripple of audits. The attacker therefore pays real capital and audit exposure for each fake identity, even when its sonnet of fabricated activity looks convincing.
